subject: Residency & Logs: pinning scenarios, cross-region backups — post-call action items
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Cheng <laura@optisystem.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-29T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up: residency & logging items from today's call

Thanks again for taking the time today, Laura — good discussion. Below is a short recap and the action items we agreed on so we have a clear path forward. Let me know if I missed anything.

Recap (high level):
- OptiSystem wants EU-first residency for production traffic, with the ability to fail over to US and APAC for availability.
- Primary concerns: PII exposure in logs, log retention windows, evidence for encryption/SOC2, and how backups/snapshots cross regions.
- OptiSystem security team requested examples of log redaction and a retention matrix mapped to data types.

Action items we committed to:
1) Share a concise matrix for log types (audit, request/response, error traces) and typical retention options (30/90/365 days) + how sensitive fields can be redacted at ingest. See attached "log-retention-matrix.xlsx".
2) Provide a regional pinning/playbook draft showing: EU pin primary, warm-standby US, APAC cold backup, and the failover triggers and expected RPO/RTO estimates. Attached: "redwood-residency-options.pdf".
3) Confirm whether payloads or logs contain PII by default and outline our redaction and minimization options.
4) Provide evidence links for encryption at rest (customer-managed KMS) and SOC2 artifact locations — will post links to Drive and HubSpot.

Quick technical notes (for your architects):
- Pinning: customers can pin by region or by availability zone affinity. We support weighted pinning (e.g., 95% EU, 5% US warm standby).
- Failover: warm-standby means Kafka-backed requests buffer + pre-warmed model instances in target region. Typical RPO: 5-15 minutes depending on queue depth; RTO: 5-20 minutes depending on model size and KV cache warm-up.
- Logs: ingest-level redaction can drop or mask configured JSON fields; token-level obfuscation is available as an add-on.

Next steps: I'll wait for the security team to confirm one representative question set; in the meantime I'll loop Ben and Karthik to produce the short playbook + an options-based pricing estimate.

Attachments: redwood-residency-options.pdf, log-retention-matrix.xlsx

Best,
Mina Haddad

Thanks, Mina — that recap helps. A few clarifying questions from our side (security team copied):

1) Scope of PII in logs: are request/response bodies logged by default? If so, which fields (full payload vs. selected fields)? We need an architecture diagram showing where redaction would occur (edge vs. ingest).
2) Retention: we typically need 7/30/180/365 windows by data category; can you confirm whether we can set this per-route or is it tenant-level only?
3) Cross-region backups: how are model snapshots and customer datastore backups replicated? Are snapshots encrypted with CMK (customer-managed key)? Where is key material stored (cloud KMS vs. HSM)?
4) Failover behaviour: if EU becomes unavailable, is there an automatic promote or manual failover? What is the DNS propagation and routing strategy?
5) Logs containing user identifiers: is there an off-the-shelf redaction policy (PII patterns) and a guarantee you won't keep full-text beyond the retention setting?

Deliverables we need before a security review:
- Short playbook (1-2 pages) that shows EU-primary + failover sequence and estimated RPO/RTO numbers.
- Log retention matrix by category and a sample redaction config we can drop into our ingress rules.
- Link to SOC2 evidence or a summary of controls for encryption/key management.

We think this looks promising; after we validate with security we plan to schedule a short architecture review next week.

--Laura

Laura — thanks, great list. Answers inline below, and I've attached a short draft playbook (regional-playbook.md) with diagrams and the retention matrix already attached.

1) Scope of PII in logs:
- Defaults: we log request metadata (timestamps, route, model, token counts) and anonymized request IDs. We do NOT persist full request/response bodies by default for hosted tenants unless customer enables "debug" logging.
- Redaction: ingest-time redaction supports JSON path rules and regex patterns; we can drop or mask fields (email, ssn, name) before any storage. Token-level obfuscation can be enabled for higher assurance.

2) Retention granularity:
- Config: per-tenant and per-route retention tiers are supported. You can set different windows per route (e.g., /search = 30d, /support = 365d).
- Defaults: 30 days for request metadata, 90 days for coarse analytics summaries; adjustable via Console or API.

3) Snapshots & backups:
- Model snapshots: stored in region of primary pin; cross-region replication is optional and uses encrypted transfer. Snapshots are encrypted with CMK; we support customer-managed KMS keys (AWS KMS, GCP Cloud KMS, or HSM integration).
- Datastore backups: can be configured to replicate to a hold-only cold bucket in APAC/US as needed, encrypted with CMK. Key material remains in the cloud KMS unless you request HSM-based storage — we can provide an HSM option for Private deployments.

4) Failover behaviour:
- We offer both automatic and manual failover policies. Automatic failover uses health-check and capacity-based triggers with weighted routing. Manual failover is available via Console for controlled cutovers.
- DNS & routing: we use multi-region Anycast + TLS SNI routing; switch-over is typically sub-60s for routing, but model cold-warm warm-up and KV cache fill add to total RTO as noted earlier.

5) Redaction guarantees:
- We will not keep full-text beyond the configured retention. Redaction occurs before persistent store writes if configured. Audit logs of redaction decisions are available (WORM option) for compliance.

Attached: regional-playbook.md (draft), redwood-residency-options.pdf, log-retention-matrix.xlsx

Proposed next step: Ben and Karthik will produce a concise options quote (EU-pin with warm US standby and APAC cold backup) and an SOW sketch — target EOD Friday. I'll coordinate the architecture review once the security team confirms availability.

Best,
Mina
